subject: RFI: Sealed environment — telemetry dataflow, operator access, and KMS integration
messages:
From: Procurement Team <procurement@caldwellhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Sealed environment — telemetry dataflow and KMS integration

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this RFI. Caldwell Health is evaluating private/on-prem deployments for highly regulated workloads. Attached is our standard sealed-environment questionnaire (RFI_Form_SealedEnv.pdf). High level asks we need covered:

- Logical dataflow for operator-facing telemetry and how we segregate patient data from observability data.
- Does Redwood store any PII or model inputs in your control plane for private deployments?
- KMS model: can Redwood integrate with our HSM-backed KMS (key import, key wrapping, rotation) or do you require Redwood-managed keys?
- Operator access model: can operator tooling be completely air-gapped (no outbound control-plane egress) while still supporting patching and support traces?

We'd like an initial reply by EOD Wednesday (PST) so we can decide whether to move to a procurement demo. Samir Rao from our security consultancy (cc) will coordinate technical follow-ups.

Attachments: RFI_Form_SealedEnv.pdf (filled by procurement team)

Best,
Anita Patel
Sr. Procurement Manager, Caldwell Health
procurement@caldwellhealth.com

Subject: Re: RFI: Sealed environment — telemetry dataflow and KMS integration

Anita — thanks, got the form. Quick clarifying notes so our reply can be precise:

1) When you say "operator-facing telemetry" are you limited to platform telemetry (GPU/OS metrics, agent health) or do you also need application-level traces that might include request metadata? We typically separate levels and can suppress payloads by default.

2) For KMS: do you require Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) with HSM key import, or is a Key-Encryption-Key (KEK) wrapping model acceptable where the customer KMS wraps Redwood-managed keys at rest?

3) Patching/support: do you have a preferred cadence for out-of-band patch bundles and is remote support limited to an operator-mediated upload (we can provide signed patch bundles you ingest)?

Irene and Vanessa — looping you both for short answers below so we can bundle a single evidence pack and clear diagrams to Caldwell. Plan: I'll assemble a telemetry dataflow diagram and a KMS compatibility matrix; can we include the operator access playbook snippet and the one-page runbook for airgap updates?

Karthik
Director, Solutions — Private Deploys
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Sealed environment — telemetry dataflow and KMS integration

Karthik — quick context from the security side: Caldwell requires physical separation of patient payloads from observability. Key requirements:

- No plaintext request or model input data may be transmitted to any hosted control plane. If logs are needed, they must be filtered client-side and redacted before egress.
- KMS MUST support HSM-backed keys with customer-controlled rotation and a way to import existing keys (or generate keys in-custody).
- Operator telemetry can be collected, but it must be tagged/partitioned and, where possible, routed to a customer-owned telemetry sink (e.g., Splunk/OnPrem Prometheus) rather than Redwood-managed storage.

Questions for Redwood: do you support a local-only telemetry sink and a "no-control-plane-telemetry" configuration? Also how do you sign patch bundles and can you provide the verification key for on-prem operator ingestion?

Samir Rao
Principal Consultant, CyberAssure
samir@cyberassure.com
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@caldwellhealth.com>, Samir Rao <samir@cyberassure.com>

Subject: Re: RFI: Sealed environment — telemetry dataflow and KMS integration

Anita / Samir — thanks for the clarifications. Attached is a concise evidence pack and our answers below. I tried to keep the technical detail executable so your architects can validate quickly. Attachments: redwood-private-deploy-telemetry-matrix.xlsx, kms-integration-diagram.pdf

High-level summary (short answers):
- Control plane: For Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments we offer an optional "control-plane proxy" pattern that allows the customer to run a minimal control-plane gateway inside their network. When enabled, Redwood does NOT persist model inputs or request payloads in our hosted control plane. Metadata-only heartbeats (service availability indicators) are optional and under customer control.

- Telemetry and observability: You can configure the runtime to emit metrics/traces exclusively to a customer-owned sink (Prometheus, OpenTelemetry collector, Splunk HEC). We provide a telemetry matrix (see attached) that maps signal categories to permitted sinks and redaction knobs. By default, request payloads and model inputs are never emitted unless explicitly enabled by the customer and gated by a redact/allowlist policy.

- KMS model: We support three integration patterns we describe in the attached diagram:
  1) BYOK with HSM import — customer imports HSM-wrapped root keys into the local KMS; Redwood's runtime uses those keys for disk encryption and key wrapping.
  2) KEK wrap — customer-managed KEK in their KMS wraps short-lived runtime keys; Redwood never sees plaintext KEK material.
  3) HSM proxy — for air-gapped sites we support an on-prem HSM-proxy process that performs crypto ops locally; the runtime calls the proxy over localhost.

We can confirm: key import, rotation (customer-driven), and HSM-backed root keys are supported in the on-prem package. We provide example integration scripts for AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM, and PKCS#11-compatible HSMs — included in the diagram attachment.

- Operator access & patching: We offer an operator-access mode where the operator tools are air-gapped. Support/patch bundles are signed using an RSA/ECDSA signature we publish; customers verify signatures before applying. For emergency debug sessions, we provide an operator-consent mechanism: a per-session ephemeral token that is generated by the customer operator and validated against the local control-plane gateway. No inbound support tunnel is required.

- Evidence & artifacts provided:
  • Telemetry mapping (attached spreadsheet) — category -> sample fields -> redaction controls -> sink options
  • KMS integration diagram (attached PDF) — shows BYOK, KEK-wrap, and HSM-proxy patterns and sample commands
  • One-page operator runbook excerpt (inlined below) for airgap patch ingestion and signature verification

Operator runbook excerpt:
1) Obtain signed patch bundle from Redwood portal (sha256 checksum published).
2) Transfer bundle to sealed environment via air-gapped media.
3) Run local verify script: ./verify_patch --bundle bundle.tar.gz --pubkey redwood_pub.pem
4) Ingest via operator CLI; CLI enforces RBAC and records an audit entry.

Next steps I propose:
- If this aligns, Vanessa can schedule a short technical walkthrough (30–45m) where we walk the KMS proxy demo and show the telemetry sink wiring.
- We'll also provide a 1-page attestation letter for your CISO describing the no-plaintext control-plane guarantee for Private deployments.

Irene / Vanessa — please review and add any clarifying notes; if Anita wants the full set of PoC scripts we can package them in a separate secure artifact link.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions — Private Deploys
Redwood Inference
